featured_reviews.review_text:
Amazing place. Way better than the Matunga south indian restaurants.

Shree Muthappan Eating House is a hidden gem at Bhandup on the Jangal Mangal Road. Appam is the speciality of this place and it is totally worth it. The appam is not the sweet round appam but the Malayalam style Appam like dosa. We also had Sada Dosa which was crispy till the last bite. Sambhar and Chutney are one of the best around Mumbai. Your meal should mandatorily end with filter coffee which has the correct amount of decoction and the required sweetness.

Other specialities are Pazham Pori(Kela Bhajji), Parotta, etc. which we couldn't try.

The hotel is clean and the staff are friendly. Owner is a good person and good to have a conversation with.

You can park your two wheelers outside the restaurant on the road.

The rates are way too economical for the quality of food served.

I would surely visit Muthappan Eating house again.

Cheers.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Bhandup Central Restaurant, and while the ambiance was just okay, the standout feature was undoubtedly the non-vegetarian tandoori items.

The decor and atmosphere were quite average, lacking any distinctive flair or charm. The seating was comfortable enough, but the overall environment felt a bit underwhelming. However, what the restaurant lacked in ambiance, it more than made up for with its delicious tandoori offerings.

The tandoori chicken was succulent and perfectly marinated, with just the right amount of spice. Each bite was a delightful explosion of flavors, cooked to perfection in the traditional tandoor oven. The lamb kebabs were equally impressive, tender and juicy with a smoky finish that left a lasting impression. The variety of tandoori dishes available catered to different palates, ensuring there was something for everyone to enjoy.

The service was efficient, and the staff were friendly and attentive, making sure our dining experience was pleasant despite the unremarkable surroundings.

In conclusion, Bhandup Central Restaurant may not win any awards for its ambiance, but it is definitely worth a visit for its excellent non-vegetarian tandoori items. If you're a fan of well-cooked, flavorful tandoori dishes, this place won't disappoint.

featured_reviews.name: siddharth dey
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mitran Da Dhaba is an amazing place if you love authentic Punjabi dhaba-style tandoor food. This is a complete dhaba experience, so I’d strongly recommend ordering their tandoor specials, parathas, and even Chinese dishes rather than Mughlai or biryanis.

The place has an open-space setup, which feels great when you’re dining with friends or family. Everything is very clean and hygienically prepared, and it really feels like there are specialized chefs handling specific dishes — the taste clearly reflects their expertise. Portions are very generous, so you definitely get good value for money.

All tandoori dishes are outstanding and cooked live in front of you, which adds to the experience. Must-try items include Reshmi Kebab, Kheema Paratha, Chicken Fried Rice, White Makhan Tandoori Chicken, and of course the Gulab Jamuns, which are absolutely amazing.

Parking is convenient — you can park your car or bike on the opposite side of the road, and since there’s usually no traffic jam after 8 PM, it’s quite hassle-free. Do note that menu prices are exclusive of GST, so factor that in while ordering.

Weekends can get crowded, but weekday evenings are comfortable and much less busy, making it a perfect time for a relaxed dinner.

Overall, a must-visit dhaba for tandoor lovers! 🔥🍗

featured_reviews.review_text:
Before visiting Shera 2.0, I would recommend reading this review.

**1. Limited AC Seating**
If your group has 7 or more people and you're planning to sit in the AC section, be aware that the AC room is quite small. A single table can accommodate a maximum of around 6 people comfortably. Larger groups may not be able to sit together inside. During the summer season, sitting outside for a long time can also be uncomfortable.

**2. Outdoor Seating & Mosquitoes**
Since the AC seating is limited, many guests may have to sit outside. During our visit, there were quite a lot of mosquitoes, which made the experience even more uncomfortable. If you're visiting in the evening, especially during warmer months, this is something to keep in mind.

**3. Food Taste**
We visited this place after watching several reels and expected something unique. However, the food tasted pretty average and was no different from what you can find at many other restaurants. In fact, you can get similar food quality and taste at several places for a much lower price.

**4. Slow Service**
Make sure to place your order as early as possible because the waiting time is extremely long. Every order we placed took around 40–45 minutes to reach our table.

**5. Overpriced Menu**
If you're visiting thinking this is a budget-friendly dhaba, you may be disappointed. The pricing is surprisingly high. For example:

* Mojito: ₹499
* Fresh Lime Soda: ₹399

Considering the overall experience, the prices felt excessive.

**6. Staff Attitude**
Our bill was around ₹20,000 for a group of 10 people. We politely asked if any discount was available, but the staff's response felt quite rude and dismissive. It seemed as if asking a simple question was somehow inappropriate.

**Overall Experience**
From the moment we arrived, the overall vibe of the place didn't feel welcoming. Unfortunately, we had to stay due to the circumstances. Between the limited seating, mosquitoes, slow service, average food, high prices, and disappointing customer service, the overall experience did not justify the hype.

**Rating: 1/5**

featured_reviews.name: dhawal gala
featured_reviews.review_text:
Stepping into Bayroute in Cuffe Parade is less like walking into a restaurant and more like embarking on an enchanting journey across the Mediterranean and Middle East. From the moment you cross the threshold, the attention to detail in the ambience, the authentic depth of the cuisine, and the seamless service work in perfect harmony to deliver an unforgettable fine-dining experience.

The Ambience: An Arabian Night's Dream
The ambience at Bayroute is truly its soul, beautifully capturing the old-world charm and opulence of the Levant. The decor is a magnificent blend of Moroccan, Turkish, and Arabian influences. Warm, rich lighting spills over intricately patterned floor tiles and tastefully adorned walls, which feature beautiful Turkish art. The seating is plush and comfortable, with Moroccan printed sofas that invite a leisurely, communal dining experience.

The entire space exudes a refined yet cozy atmosphere—perfect for a romantic evening, a sophisticated family dinner, or celebrating a special occasion. It’s an aesthetically curated masterpiece where every corner offers a visual delight, transporting you far away from the hustle of Mumbai.

The Food: An Authentic and Flavorful Expedition
The menu is an extensive map of culinary delights from countries like Egypt, Turkey, Lebanon, and Greece. It's a testament to authentic, well-researched cuisine, and every dish we tried was a revelation.The ingredients taste fresh, and the authentic spices are used with a delicate hand, ensuring the dishes are flavorful without being overwhelmingly heavy.

The Service: Courteous and Impeccable

A superb meal is only elevated by excellent service, and Bayroute truly shines here. The staff is exceptionally courteous, knowledgeable, and attentive. Our server was well-versed in the menu, offering insightful recommendations and patiently explaining the different regional nuances of the dishes. The pacing of the meal was perfect—neither rushed nor slow—allowing us to fully enjoy the experience. The attention to detail, from refreshing water glasses to clearing plates promptly, was seamless and professional.

Bayrute is more than just a restaurant; it’s a cultural experience. While it is on the higher end of the pricing scale, the unparalleled ambience, the authentic and delicious food, and the impeccable, friendly service make it absolutely worth the indulgence. It remains a must-visit destination for anyone looking to sample the finest Middle Eastern and Mediterranean cuisine in Mumbai in a truly magnificent setting.

featured_reviews.name: Monica
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re craving an authentic Middle Eastern experience in Mumbai, BAYROUTE is a place you simply can’t miss. We visited their Cuffe Parade outlet, and honestly, it felt like stepping straight into an Arabian dining room, warm, inviting, and rich in flavours.

Let’s start with their Classic Hummus, because that’s a non-negotiable order here. Creamy, smooth, and beautifully balanced, it’s topped with pine nuts, finished with labneh, and generously drizzled with good quality extra virgin olive oil. Simple, classic, and done perfectly, exactly how hummus should be.

For a refreshing sip, we tried their Reyhan, a soft beverage made with muddled orange and basil. Super refreshing, fragrant, and a great palate cleanser alongside the heavier dishes.

The Cheese Manakeesh was another standout. A soft Middle Eastern flatbread brushed with olive oil, loaded with lots of cheese. Comforting, indulgent, and perfect for sharing.

One of the highlights of the meal was the Dijaj Tria, a roasted trio of chicken kebabs featuring harissa spiced chicken, creamy shish taouk and Saffron Joojeh, served with garlic sauce, spicy schug and a punchy acili ezme dip. Every skewer brought something different to the table, and all of them were cooked beautifully.

Seafood lovers will enjoy the Butter Garlic Prawns, juicy, well-seasoned, and finished with rich garlic butter flavours without overpowering the prawns themselves.

We wrapped up with the Yemeni Mandi, which was aromatic, flavourful, and comforting, a wholesome dish that truly completes the Middle Eastern feast.

Overall, BAYROUTE delivers a genuine Arabian dining experience, from flavours to ambience. Perfect for anyone who enjoys Lebanese, Turkish, and Middle Eastern cuisine under one roof.

featured_reviews.name: Adil Syed
featured_reviews.review_text:
Location & Popularity
Bagdadi is located in a prime area of Colaba, making it easily accessible and always buzzing with people. The restaurant is extremely popular, especially during evening hours, which clearly reflects its strong reputation among food lovers.

Waiting Time
Due to the heavy rush during peak hours, particularly in the evenings, customers usually have to wait for their turn. While the wait can be a bit long, it also speaks volumes about how loved the food here is.

Food Quality
The food at Bagdadi is genuinely great. The flavors are rich, consistent, and worth coming back for. It’s one of those places where the taste truly lives up to the hype.

Ambience & Renovation (Personal Opinion)
In my personal opinion, the restaurant could really benefit from a renovation. The place feels a bit dated, and a refresh would greatly enhance the dining experience without taking away from its old-school charm.

Final Verdict
Bagdadi is a must-visit for its excellent food and prime Colaba location. Despite the waiting time and the need for renovation, the taste and authenticity make it well worth the experience—especially for those who don’t mind a little wait for good food.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Let's start with the 40 minute wait. When you're made to wait that long, you naturally expect something rewarding at the end of it...The ambience was good, and after waiting so long to get a table, we were genuinely happy to finally be seated. The place is moderately expensive, and honestly, nobody mind paying a premium if the experience justifies it. Unfortunately, the service here was pathetic

My friend asked for a bottle of water and specifically requested one at normal temperature. Even after more than 30 minutes, it didn't arrive. When it finally did, they brought chilled water instead. I understand weekends are busy and service may take longer than usual, but taking that much time for a simple bottle of water is ridiculous

Not wanting to waste any more time, we ordered Masala Papad. When it arrived, it had no sev on it. Upon asking, we were casually told that they didn't have available. At the prices you're charging, are customers supposed to simply accept a poorer experience without question?

Then came the next masterpiece. One of my friends ordered a Diet Coke. After waiting more than 10 minutes, the waiter brought a regular Coke. At that point, all of us started laughing because it had become almost comical. When we asked whether they even had Diet Coke, he confidently said they did. The problem was that he had already opened the regular can before asking to change it.

Unfortunately, the experience didn't stop there. We ordered Tandoori Rotis, and the first round arrived burnt to the point that they looked like coal. We told the waiter and politely requested that the next be made properly. The second round arrived looking exactly the same. When we pointed it out, the waiter simply replied, "Weekend hai sir, ho jata hai"

For God's sake, man, we're here to enjoy our weekend too. Why are you ruining the experience?

Throughout the evening, we kept laughing at all the things that kept going wrong because otherwise it would have been frustrating. But when the bill arrived, I genuinely felt compelled to write this review. I rarely leave negative reviews and have never written one this harsh before, but this experience left me with no choice :,)

featured_reviews.name: Sanchit Kamath
featured_reviews.review_text:
Located at Colaba Causeway, this mughlai place is a pretty old and one of the legendary eateries which the city has to offer

The place has a royal ambiance but i believe they are definitely in a need of upgrade now.. especially the upper floors. The service is good.. initially it took a while for them to serve us as there was a huge corporate group having their party but once they had their attention to us.. they made sure that we are served well!

We went there for lunch, we ordered:
1) Roomali Roti: The roti was literally soft like a cushion and melts in your mouth, this is one of the best Roomali roti I have ever had.

2) Chicken Bhuna: Made on tawa, this boneless chicken bhuna was actually delicious. Chicken cooked was soft and melting in my mouth whereas the masala had right amount of spices to it and wasn't spicy which was to my liking!

3) Chicken Tikka Biryani: Usually the highlight of the restaurant, but to my surprise the biryani was better than what I had 1.5 years ago as it seems their chef has changed. The last time when I had it, the chicken was really dry and had been marinated in red color.. though it was charred well but was too dry! Whereas this time the tikka was properly marinated and grilled to the right amount leaving the chicken juicy and tender. The quantity served was good too. The rice i believe could have been more fluffier.

4) Sweet Fresh lime soda: The lemon concentrate at the bottom mixed with sugar and added soda.. mixed well.. definitely was refreshing but i wish they could add the fresh lemon juice for better taste.

Overall, a good place to have your fulfilling dinner.. the place had originally introduced to me by my mother.. though it might have changed over the time but still manages to have the same pull!
